1) We need confirmation of the order you prefer for: SCCs (EU), UK IDTA / UK Addendum, and the TIA/DTIA scoping — specifically which documents you expect signed first and which can be executed in parallel.
2) A concise list of evidence items Redwood will provide for the TIA (logs, subprocessors, encryption attestations, sample retention config).

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Sequencing SCCs / UK Addendum + TIA scope for Lumen Health

Jordan — thanks, and good question. High level sequencing we recommend (and can accelerate if you need):

- Step 1 (same day): Execute the base DPA with SCCs (EU Standard Contractual Clauses) attached as an appendix. This gives immediate contractual safeguards for EU controllers/processors.
- Step 2 (within 48 hours): Execute the UK Addendum / UK IDTA. We typically surface the UK addendum immediately after the SCCs are in place — legal teams often sign these in quick succession.
- Step 3 (T+0 to T+5 working days): Finalize TIA/DTIA scope and evidence handoff. The TIA is scoped with the information in the DPA and subprocessor map; it's typically a follow-on technical attestation rather than a blocker for service commencement.

Attachments I'm sharing now to speed review:  
- Redwood_TIA_Scoping_v1.pdf (scope, evidence list, sample templates)
- RW_Subprocessor_Map_Q3_2027.csv (current subprocessors & roles)
- DPA_UK_Addendum_Draft.docx (redlineable draft of the addendum)

Quick notes on evidence we can provide for the TIA (full list in the PDF):
- Audit logs (sampling window) and retention policy statement
- Subprocessor list + contact & contractual tiering
- Encryption at rest/in transit descriptions and key management approach (KMS providers, rotation cadence)
- Data residency routing controls and fallback behavior (region routing policy)
- SOC 2 summary + most recent readiness checklist (we can provide the attestation once NDA/LOU is in place)

Kimberly & Laura — looping you in for technical/evidence timing and for the UK addendum legal finalization. Jordan, happy to get on a short call if you want to work through sequencing live.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Sales (Compliance Accounts)
Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail from the infra side — items we typically include in the TIA evidence bundle and an estimated delivery cadence: 

- System architecture diagram (redacted PII flows): 1 business day to prepare a version for legal review.
- Subprocessor controls matrix (access, MFA, key custody): available now (see attached CSV) but will add classified control statements in 2 BD.
- KV cache & on-device caching behavior + sample latency profiles: 2-3 BD for stakeholder review.
- Sample audit log export (30-day window): we can pull a schema + 14-day sample within 2 BD; full 90-day slice requires SOC/Ops approval.
- KMS integration notes (providers and rotation): immediate summary, formal key custody attestation in 3 BD.

Operational ask: Jordan — do you have a prioritized list of which evidence buckets your security reviewers need first (e.g., logs vs. subprocessor controls)? We can stage delivery to get you what your team needs to unblock procurement.

—Kimberly
Senior Infrastructure Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Jordan — I've taken Monica's draft and made a couple of minor edits to the UK Addendum language to clarify routing fallback and processor cooperation clauses. Planned next steps from legal:  

1) We'll send the DPA + SCCs as a single package for signature first thing this afternoon.
2) UK Addendum will be attached as a second document inline with the DPA package; signers can execute both in the same DocuSign envelope if you prefer (we recommend that to simplify procurement).
3) TIA scoping and evidence transfer will proceed as a companion activity — it does not need to be fully complete to sign the DPA/UK Addendum, but we will lock the TIA acceptance criteria within 5 business days after signature.

DocuSign link will be shared when the envelope is created. Please let us know if Lumen's procurement requires separate sign-off steps — happy to stage differently.

Regards,
